title: ReproCheck Evidence Trial v19
research_question: On unseen public ML result claims, does access to raw artifacts and deterministic recomputation improve contradiction recall over report-only and supplied-metric review without exceeding a 5% false-accusation rate?

hypotheses.h1: Raw recomputation improves contradiction recall over report-only review by at least 10 percentage points with a positive owner-cluster bootstrap lower bound.
hypotheses.h2: Raw recomputation preserves a false-accusation rate at or below 5%.
hypotheses.certificate_track: Minimal witnesses preserve verdicts, reduce bytes, and reject registered tampering.

source_frame.population: Public GitHub ML result claims with immutable commits and retrievable evidence
source_frame.selection: Deterministic salted ordering, one included repository per owner, preregistered exclusions

scientific_boundary: This preregistered trial can support a bounded claim about one frozen public-source frame. It cannot prove universal ML reproducibility, causality, or performance on private and non-GitHub research artifacts.
